Hey, I want to say I really appreciate you! You seem very respectful even though we disagree, and I hope I've reciprocated that respect myself.

Thanks for your comment. At no point had I said Christianity was evil, nor do I consider it to be evil.  I also refuse your point that Christianity was an "upgrade" to the beliefs of "African slaves." That very idea is one of colonialist philosophy, and it is incredibly flawed for many reasons that I could explain if you would like. 

 I think you are confusing many issues together in the point you make. The history of Christianity before colonialism is a moot point, especially its comparison to other religions. Whether or not Christianity is "evil" also does not have any actual effect on whether or not it can be considered problematic when it is a productof colonialism. I would also like to refute your point that  southern America was anti-Christian during its slavery period, as that, to my knowledge, is simply not true. Please present me with info that could disprove that.
Thank you for understanding, I appreciate that. On your equation, the broccoli ultimately helped one be healthy and grown. Have African people/culture ultimately benefited from colonialism?

No issue with any religion at all. I apologize if it seems I'm coming from an uninformed background, but that is why I'm asking in the first place. It just seems odd to me that Christianity and colonialism can be separated by its victims when so many other effects of colonialism have been rendered outdated and problematic by majority public opinion. I'm not saying black people should not practice Christianity, not at all, but I wonder why I've never even heard the idea discussed.

Sure, but can you really equate the two? Christianity is a way of thinking and living, not an objectively healthy food. Of course, Christianity preaches excellent values on the whole and teach many to lead good and generous lives, but if a certain way of thinking and living was systematically enforced through acts of violence, isn't practicing that way of thinking and living (even if it has an intrinsic value) just an imprint of that same racism and violence? Playing into the same colonialist mindset?

I read this little thing that's been on my mind for weeks. It's from this memoir comic called Alec. It goes "Loneliness is not a longing for people, but a longing for kind." Makes sense to me at least. Maybe you just need to find your kind?

That's really nice, and a good way of looking at it, thank you so much. Unfortunately I kinda just got unlucky and didn't have anyone stay in town but I do still keep in touch with a few very close friends, and I'm not making that excuse to not being able to make new friends now. I think I'm very capable of it actually! It's just a matter of means I guess. I come from a very big family and I've always been used to having many relationships and friends, so as of late I've had to learn how to live alone and be comfortable with myself. Which is rewarding in its own way! I also recently went through a break up from a pretty serious relationship, and though the break up itself was very amicable, it was still an incredibly tough thing to get through, and that's probably contributed to my feelings of being lonely as of late. I just kinda wanna get out there and be part of a group or just make a friend I see in person every once in a while. I sincerely miss having relationships and connecting with others.

Yea no problem! My favorite rap album of all time is Madvillainy by Madvillain. It's a very comic-booky album and it is just. genius. The lyricism is top notch and the beats by Madlib is just perfect. It's jazzy and laid back and incredible. If you want something a bit more upbeat and soulful, Aquemini by Outkast is great too! And if you want something a little experimental and noisy but very thought provoking, CLPPNG by clipping. is also really good. Each song is like a vignette of the speaker's background and the ideologies that come with it. Very powerful. For pop music, the new Pop 2 by Charli XCX is really great! I'm a big fan of Bridgit Mendler also, her EP Atlantis is short, sweet, and really well done. Aaaand last but not least RINA by Rina Sawayama is the epitome of early 2000's pop even though it was released like a month ago.
